headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write files and use shell while dbt-core reads warehouse data, creating default-path leakage and workflow conflicts; no direct prompt-injection bridge is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can use the filesystem and shell, but dbt-core exposes only warehouse/API surfaces and no shared channel or parser bridge is documented. The pairwise prompt-injection path is therefore not evidenced beyond an unusual manual copy-paste or file handoff, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies AutoGPT output into dbt-core inputs or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same untrusted text file, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep outputs in separate directories.
Do not copy-paste agent output into dbt inputs without review.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
Add a human approval step before any dbt run.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and make allowlisted network calls, while dbt-core touches data warehouse data. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could move warehouse data into AutoGPT context and then out through its networked workflow. This is plausible in default operator setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing warehouse extracts, leakage is plausible.
IF AutoGPT is given dbt-generated files or logs, those contents can be forwarded in later outputs.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Restrict AutoGPT to non-sensitive sample data.
Disable sharing of dbt logs and artifacts.
Review outbound destinations for AutoGPT.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on shared files.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT has shell and subprocess execution plus filesystem access, while dbt-core interacts with a data warehouse. Even without explicit write scopes on dbt-core, both can mutate shared project files or warehouse state through the same workflow, creating coordination conflicts in default multi-step use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory, file conflicts are possible.
IF AutoGPT triggers dbt runs while also editing project files, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign one writer per directory.
Serialize dbt runs behind a lock file.
Use separate branches for AutoGPT edits.
Review generated SQL before execution.
requires-engineering: add transactional orchestration around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate plans, code, or facts that dbt-core may consume as warehouse-facing transformations. Because dbt-core is a data-engineering tool and no verification boundary is documented, erroneous AutoGPT output can cascade into incorrect models or runs. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes AutoGPT-produced SQL or config without review, errors cascade.
IF AutoGPT is allowed to author transformation logic, downstream runs may propagate mistakes.
mitigations: Require code review for generated SQL.
Run dbt in dry-run or compile mode first.
Compare outputs against a known-good baseline.
Limit AutoGPT to drafting, not executing, transformations.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core explicitly touches data warehouse data, while AutoGPT has filesystem and network capabilities that could move regulated data into broader processing. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so this is a data-handling mismatch risk rather than a proven breach. The other agent is cited because the pairwise flow is the concern.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and is copied into AutoGPT artifacts, compliance obligations may expand.
IF retention settings differ between warehouse exports and AutoGPT logs, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Classify warehouse extracts before sharing.
Redact regulated fields from shared artifacts.
Set short retention on AutoGPT logs.
Confirm data residency for any exported files.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
